grab.definition: To take hold of something quickly and firmly with your hand.
grab.exampleUsage: Let me grab my coat and keys before we head outside.

hold.definition: To keep and support something in your hands or arms.
hold.exampleUsage: Please hold the child's hand while crossing the busy street.

grip.definition: To hold something very tightly and firmly so it does not slip.
grip.exampleUsage: Grip the handle of the hammer firmly before tapping the nail.

clutch.definition: To hold onto something tightly with your hands, often out of urgency or care.
clutch.exampleUsage: The traveler continued to clutch his ticket stub in his hand.

grasp.definition: To reach out and take a firm hold of an object with your fingers.
grasp.exampleUsage: Use both hands to grasp the rope before pulling it.

squeeze.definition: To press something firmly from opposite sides with your fingers or hand.
squeeze.exampleUsage: Squeeze half a fresh lemon over the grilled fish.

clench.definition: To close your fingers tightly into a ball or press your teeth together.
clench.exampleUsage: Take a deep breath and relax your hands if you clench your fists.

pinch.definition: To squeeze a small amount of something tightly between your thumb and finger.
pinch.exampleUsage: Add a small pinch of salt and black pepper to the soup.

carry.definition: To hold something in your hands or arms while moving it from one place to another.
carry.exampleUsage: Let me help you carry those heavy grocery bags upstairs.

lift.definition: To raise something from a lower position to a higher one using your hands.
lift.exampleUsage: Two workers worked together to lift the wooden table.

push.definition: To press against something with your hands to move it away from you.
push.exampleUsage: Push the heavy wooden door gently to open it.

pull.definition: To take hold of something and draw it toward yourself.
pull.exampleUsage: Pull the handle toward you to open the cupboard drawer.

drag.definition: To pull something heavy along the ground with effort.
drag.exampleUsage: Please lift the chair instead of trying to drag it across the floor.

shove.definition: To push someone or something roughly or with sudden force.
shove.exampleUsage: Wait patiently in line and never shove the people ahead of you.

tug.definition: To pull something hard with one or more short, quick movements.
tug.exampleUsage: Give the knot a gentle tug to make sure it is secure.

yank.definition: To pull something with a sudden, sharp movement.
yank.exampleUsage: Do not yank the power cord by the wire when unplugging it.

press.definition: To push steadily against a button or surface with your finger or hand.
press.exampleUsage: Press the green button to start the washing machine.

twist.definition: To turn a cap, handle, or object around in a circular motion with your hand.
twist.exampleUsage: Twist the lid counterclockwise to open the glass jar.

turn.definition: To rotate a knob, key, or handle so it moves in a circle.
turn.exampleUsage: Turn the key to lock the front door before leaving.

wring.definition: To twist and squeeze wet cloth tightly to force out the water.
wring.exampleUsage: Wash the dishcloth and wring it out over the sink.

throw.definition: To send an object through the air with a quick motion of your arm and hand.
throw.exampleUsage: Throw the ball to your teammate across the court.

catch.definition: To grab and hold a moving object in the air with your hands.
catch.exampleUsage: Keep your eyes on the ball so you can catch it cleanly.

toss.definition: To throw something lightly and casually through the air.
toss.exampleUsage: Please toss the crumpled paper into the recycling bin.

pitch.definition: To throw a ball accurately toward a target or batter in a game.
pitch.exampleUsage: He practiced how to pitch the ball straight over the plate.

fling.definition: To throw or cast something quickly and with strong force.
fling.exampleUsage: Do not fling your backpack onto the floor when you come home.

hurl.definition: To throw something with great strength and speed.
hurl.exampleUsage: Athletes in the field event hurl a heavy metal disc as far as they can.

lob.definition: To throw or hit a ball in a high, slow arc through the air.
lob.exampleUsage: The tennis player decided to lob the ball high over the net.

pass.definition: To hand or throw something to another person.
pass.exampleUsage: Could you please pass the bread basket across the table?

drop.definition: To let something fall from your hand to the ground.
drop.exampleUsage: Hold the glass plate with both hands so you do not drop it.

juggle.definition: To keep several balls or objects in the air at once by tossing and catching them.
juggle.exampleUsage: With practice, he learned to juggle three oranges at the same time.

touch.definition: To put your hand or fingers lightly onto someone or something.
touch.exampleUsage: Do not touch the stove while the burner is still hot.

tap.definition: To hit or touch a surface lightly and quickly with your fingers.
tap.exampleUsage: Please tap gently on the door before entering the office.

poke.definition: To push into something quickly with a finger or a pointed tool.
poke.exampleUsage: Use a wooden toothpick to poke the cake and see if it is baked.

stroke.definition: To move your hand gently and smoothly over a surface or soft fur.
stroke.exampleUsage: The child reached out to stroke the kitten's soft fur.

pat.definition: To touch someone or something gently several times with a flat hand.
pat.exampleUsage: The father smiled and gave his son an encouraging pat on the shoulder.

rub.definition: To move your hands back and forth firmly over a surface.
rub.exampleUsage: Rub your hands together with soap for twenty seconds.

scratch.definition: To rub the skin with your fingernails to relieve an itch.
scratch.exampleUsage: Try not to scratch the mosquito bite on your arm.

tickle.definition: To touch someone lightly with your fingers to make them laugh.
tickle.exampleUsage: Grandmother likes to tickle the baby's feet to make him giggle.

caress.definition: To touch a child's head or cheek gently with care and affection.
caress.exampleUsage: The mother reached out to caress her sleeping baby's cheek.

massage.definition: To rub and knead muscles with the hands to relieve tension and pain.
massage.exampleUsage: A physical therapist can massage a sore shoulder to ease the pain.

write.definition: To form letters, words, or notes on paper using a pen or pencil.
write.exampleUsage: Please write your full name at the top of the exam sheet.

draw.definition: To create a picture or diagram using a pencil, pen, or crayon.
draw.exampleUsage: The art student used charcoal to draw a mountain landscape.

paint.definition: To apply colored liquid to paper, canvas, or a wall using a brush.
paint.exampleUsage: We bought brushes and rollers to paint the bedroom walls.

type.definition: To write text by pressing the keys on a computer keyboard.
type.exampleUsage: She can type sixty words per minute on her laptop.

fold.definition: To bend paper or cloth neatly so that one part covers another.
fold.exampleUsage: Fold the letter in half before placing it inside the envelope.

tear.definition: To pull paper or cloth apart into pieces with your hands.
tear.exampleUsage: Tear a sheet of lined paper from your notebook.

cut.definition: To divide or trim paper, cloth, or food using scissors or a knife.
cut.exampleUsage: Use safety scissors to cut along the dotted line.

glue.definition: To join two pieces of paper, wood, or material together with adhesive.
glue.exampleUsage: Glue the printed label onto the front of the folder.

sew.definition: To join or repair cloth using a needle and thread.
sew.exampleUsage: My grandmother taught me how to sew a button onto a shirt.

knit.definition: To make warm clothing such as scarves or sweaters from yarn using long needles.
knit.exampleUsage: In winter, she likes to knit wool scarves for her grandchildren.
